sentences.text: Aphrosaurus was a large and highly derived plesiosaur.
No skull remains have been found for this animal.
A deepened ventral notch on the cervical vertebrae is a unique trait distinguishing Aphrosaurus from other species.
The right forelimb of the holotype shows severe distortion likely caused by a disease or injury the animal suffered while alive.
Five different genera of mosasaurs have been found in the same formation as Aphrosaurus.
The species Aphrosaurus furlongi was named by Welles in 1943.
The holotype specimen was found in 1939 in the Moreno Formation of Fresno County, California, by rancher Frank C. Piava.
Studies suggest Aphrosaurus traveled via gliding over long distances with low agility.
Aphrosaurus likely ate small prey that were ground up by gastroliths.
Phylogenetic studies place Aphrosaurus within the Weddellonectia clade but outside the Aristonectinae.
Aphrosaurus lived during the Maastrichtian stage.
The Moreno Formation, where Aphrosaurus fossils were found, dates to the early Maastrichtian and consists of turbidite, sandstone, and shale.
A second specimen initially thought to be a juvenile of Aphrosaurus was later removed from the genus due to systemic differences.
Researchers rejected the idea that a second specimen was a juvenile of Aphrosaurus because differences could not be explained by growth.
